South Indian Bank Q2 result: Profit rises 21% to ₹426 cr, gross NPAs fall
items.summary:
South Indian Bank on Thursday reported a 21 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 426 crore for the second quarter ended September 30.
The Kerala-based private sector bank registered a net profit of Rs 351 crore in the September quarter of the previous fiscal year.
Its total income increased to Rs 3,264 crore in the second quarter from Rs 2,923 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal year, South Indian Bank said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income also climbed to Rs 2,796 crore in the September quarter of FY27 from Rs 2,407 crore in the year-ago period.
On the asset quality front, gross non-performing assets (NPAs) moderated to 1.24 per cent of gross advances at the end of September 2026 against 2.93 per cent a year ago.
Similarly, net NPAs or bad loans improved to 0.09 per cent at the end of September 2026 from 0.56 per cent at the end of the same month a year earlier.

items.summary:
Indian Bank on Thursday reported a 15 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 3,462 crore for the second quarter ended September 30.
The Chennai-based public sector lender posted a net profit of Rs 3,018 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal.
Its total income increased to Rs 23,059 crore in the second quarter from Rs 19,077 crore a year ago, Indian Bank said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income rose to Rs 19,106 crore in the September quarter of FY27 from Rs 16,590 crore in the year-ago period.
The operating profit also increased to Rs 7,090 crore against Rs 4,837 crore in the same quarter a year ago.
In terms of asset quality, gross non-performing assets (NPAs) of the bank moderated to 1.61 per cent of gross advances at the end of September 2026 compared to 2.6 per cent a year ago.
Similarly, net NPAs or bad loans came down to 0.14 per cent at the end of September 2026 compared to 0.16 per cent at the end of September 2025.

items.title: BHEL Q2FY27 results: Net profit jumps over two-fold to ₹821 crore
items.summary:
State-owned BHEL on Wednesday reported a two-fold jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 820.94 crore for the September quarter, driven by higher income from key business verticals such as power and industry.
BHEL is India's largest engineering and manufacturing enterprise in the energy and infrastructure sector.
The company had clocked a net profit of Rs 374.89 crore in the second quarter of the preceding financial year, BHEL said in an exchange filing.
In July-September, the company's total income rose 24 per cent to Rs 9,553.01 crore from Rs 7,686.11 crore in the year-ago period.
Sharing segment-wise break-up, the company said that from power and industry businesses, it earned revenue of Rs 6,637.90 crore and Rs 2,662.45 crore, respectively, up from Rs 5,675.64 crore and 1,836.16 crore garnered from the two verticals in the September quarter of FY25.
Expenses stood at Rs 8,482.40 crore compared to Rs 7,201.54 crore a year ago.

items.summary: Biocon has finalized a global settlement and license agreement with Genentech for its drug Pebrilzo. This agreement addresses all ongoing legal disputes between the two companies in jurisdictions such as the US and Canada. Under the terms, Biocon can launch Pebrilzo in the EU and UK by early 2027 and in the US by Q3 of 2028. Other global launches are planned between 2026 and 2028, depending on regulatory approvals.
